question: Does posterior uncertainty-discounted plasticity retain its advantages across switch rates and less distinct rule families?
hypothesis: Posterior discounting can reduce memory interference without a large adaptation penalty, but may struggle when contexts are difficult to distinguish.
falsification: Report every condition; substantial recall or switch-accuracy regressions compared with the baseline are counterevidence.
metrics: phase online accuracy and log loss
first 100 predictions after each phase boundary
frozen A and B probes after each phase
notes: Exploratory matched seeds, not blind, no formal significance or resource matching. All families are binary first-order processes. The oracle sees the true context. Different phase lengths also change training exposure.
